name: Tobiah
description: Nehemiah's adversary living at the time of Exile and Return

points: When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them. It grieved our enemies. So our people feel the grief that the enemies will levy upon us, because someone is actually coming to give us a proper image of ourselves.

note.label: The Pit and Pendulum: The Slow Genocide of the Undesired

points: Sanballat and Tobiah were grieved that a man came to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

points: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hear of it, it grieves them exceedingly that a man has come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

points: “Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite”: these two were of other nations. “It grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.”

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: What is Esau out to stop? “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” Sanballat the Horonite was a Moabite, Tobiah an Ammonite.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

points: When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian hear it, they laugh them to scorn, despise them, and ask what this thing is, and whether they will rebel against the king.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

points: “But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” The other nations see us building and laugh us to scorn.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian” … “laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” This is the opposition Nehemiah faced rebuilding God’s walls.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: Tobiah the Ammonite stands by him and says that even what they build, if a fox go up on it, would break down their stone wall.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: “Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.” Whatever they build a fox can break down; they will not come up out of that rubble without us. That is because Nehemiah had told them they had no portion nor right in Jerusalem.

note.label: State of Decay

points: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites hear that the walls are going up and the breaches are being stopped, they are very wroth.

note.label: Nehemiah 4: Building With a Weapon in Hand

points: “When Sanballat, and Tobiah, and the Arabians, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites, heard that the walls of Jerusalem were made up”: brought up to date, they are mad that we got another school, that more people are repenting, that we get stronger every week. We did no harm to anybody. Just the fact that we are changing our evil ways into righteous ways is a threat to them, because they know once we repent God will be on our side and they will not be able to abuse us as they have.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

points: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of the enemies hear that the wall is built with no breach left, though the doors are not yet set on the gates, they turn to another plan.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Sanballat and Tobiah were of other nations, not Israelites, and now there is “Geshem the Arabian”, an Arab. “And the rest of our enemies”: notice what it calls them. Our enemies.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: Then Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent him: Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him. The heathen hired one of his own people to convince the leader to run and hide, so they could have matter for an evil report and reproach him. He sold his people out.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: Nehemiah perceives that the Most High had not sent Shemaiah, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to pronounce this prophecy.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah asks the Most High to think upon Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets who would have put him in fear according to their works.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: “My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works”: he prays to God to deal with these evil people, “and on the prophetess Noadiah”, a black woman who joined with them, “and the rest of the prophets”, the false prophets who tried to put him in fear and make him stop rebuilding Jerusalem.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: In those days the nobles of Judah send many letters to Tobiah, and his letters come to them.
Even inside Judah some remain tied to Tobiah, keeping a line of communication with the enemy.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: “Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah”. The nobles of Judah were the bourgeoisie, the Herodians you read of in the New Testament. Tobiah was of the other nations, “and the letters of Tobiah came unto them.” Many in Judah were sworn unto him: they wanted to be integrated with the other nations.

Nehemiah was all about segregation, because he saw what integrating with the other nations did to our people: a decayed estate, robbed and destroyed. That is why he told Sanballat and Tobiah they had no portion with us.

note.label: State of Decay

points: They report Tobiah's good deeds before Nehemiah and carry Nehemiah's words to Tobiah, and Tobiah sends letters to put him in fear.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: “Also they reported his good deeds before me”: these nobles, this black bourgeoisie, would go to Nehemiah and tell him how good Tobiah and the enemies of God were: these are good folks, good white folks, good Arab folks. “And uttered my words to him”: whatever Nehemiah said, they reported back. “And Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.”

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

points: “And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.” He cleaned it all up.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.” In the same chapter we started marrying heathenish wives, and Nehemiah went around smacking us up to correct us.

When did he lay hands on people and drag Tobiah out of the temple? Not the first time; the second time. The second coming of Nehemiah. The same with Christ: the second coming of Christ is judgment and destruction. No long talking, no pleading, no conversations: swift judgment.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come
